title: POC: payload variance SLOs & sampling playbook
summary: Scoping call to define POC success criteria and measurement plan for latency SLOs under payload variance. Next: Redwood to share sampling script, Polar to provide traffic histograms and dataset snapshots; schedule baseline run week of 2026-08-03.

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-07-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Ayesha (PTL ML), Marco (PTL Platform), Dana (PTL CTO)

Summary (auto): quick run to align on SLOs, sampling, and timeline.

00:00 Ethan: okay thanks for joining, everyone. Quick roundtable — Ethan from Redwood, Priya our platform SE, Liam joining from solutions. 
00:12 Dana: hi all, Dana here — CTO at Polar Tech Labs. We're mainly trying to lock down what success looks like for a short POC around inference economics and latency at scale. 
00:20 Ayesha: a quick note, we have pretty wide payload variance, from tiny prompts (10-40 tokens) to fat batch jobs embedding ~4k tokens, plus multi-instruction chat. So need to make sure we measure both first token and per-token. 
00:31 Priya: yeah that's exactly the challenge. We wanted this call to define payload buckets, SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), and how we'll sample. Can you give a bit more on your traffic shape? 
00:44 Marco: rough numbers — 70% of calls are short Q/A single-turn (mean 32 tokens), 20% are medium interactive flows (200-600 tokens), and 10% are long batch-ish requests up to 4k tokens. There's also spikes from nightly inference jobs. 
00:58 Liam: are those batch jobs synchronous from clients or queued? 
01:01 Marco: currently they run sync from our internal batch runner, but we can re-run them in replay for the POC. 
01:08 Ethan: great. Let's propose three payload classes: small (<64 tokens), medium (64-1024 tokens), large (>1024 tokens). For each class we should define TTFT p95/p99 and TPOT p95/p99 targets. Those will be our acceptance criteria. 
01:22 Dana: what are realistic targets? We care about user-facing latency for small requests and cost/throughput for large ones. 
01:28 Priya: from similar customers we benchmark a TTFT p95 target of 200-300ms on dedicated GPUs for small payloads; p99 is often in the 350-450ms range depending on KV cache warm state. For TPOT, customers usually measure steady-state per-token cost and throughput — a TPOT p95 target of 180-220ms per 1k tokens in mixed batching scenarios is reasonable, though that's fuzzy. 
01:51 Ayesha: that seems optimistic for our stack, we run on self-hosted k8s and have network overheads. Also we use customer-side encryption TLS + internal proxies. 
02:02 Priya: good point. We'll factor in e2e instrumentation — for measurement we suggest separating network/client time and runtime time. Redwood can provide measurement hooks for server-side TTFT and per-token times; you'll capture client-side RTT as well. 
02:18 Marco: how do we measure TTFT exactly? Some vendors report from request receive to first byte, others include queue time. We need a clear definition. 
02:27 Liam: agreed. Proposed definitions: TTFT = time from request arrival at Redwood ingress to first token emitted (server‑side). TPOT = time to emit the final token divided by total tokens (steady-state per-token metric), measured on server side. We'll also capture end-to-end latency separately. 
02:42 Dana: ok, and cold-starts? The nightly jobs cause cold KV caches. Should we measure warm vs cold p99? 
02:50 Priya: yes, include both warm and cold cases in the playbook. For cold we measure TTFT with an empty KV cache; for warm we measure after a 5‑minute sustained run.
02:59 Ayesha: sampling plan — we prefer a hybrid approach: replay a week of production requests plus synthetic sweeps to exercise extremes. 
03:08 Ethan: exactly. Our suggested approach: 1) Collect payload histograms and a 7‑day sample of actual requests (metadata only; no PII) 2) Create three synthetic traffic profiles matching short/medium/long proportions 3) Run production replay for functional parity and synthetic stress tests (ramp, steady-state, spike).
03:25 Marco: can Redwood share the sampling script? We want something we can run on our side to scrub and export. 
03:29 Priya: yes we'll share a python script with sampling knobs and a playbook. We'll include example JMX-style scenarios: steady 200 RPS small, 50 RPS mixed, and burst 400 RPS for 30s. Link: https://redwood.internal/samples/payload-playbook (note: placeholder). 
03:48 Dana: for acceptance criteria — are we comfortable with asymmetrical targets per bucket? For small: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 420ms. For medium: TTFT p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 700ms. For large: TPOT p95 <= 300ms per 1k tokens and end-to-end job completion p95 <= 4s for common 2k token jobs. 
04:12 Ethan: that's a good starting point. Redwood's recommendation is to pick conservative p99s for cold starts and p95s for steady-state. Also include SLOs for error rates and tail dropout. 
04:24 Ayesha: error budget — what level do you expect during the POC? 
04:27 Liam: for a 2‑week POC, we don't enforce strict commercial SLAs, but acceptance should allow a small error budget: error rate <= 0.5% and no more than one critical outage. 
04:36 Marco: instrumentations — what metrics should we capture in the dashboard? 
04:39 Priya: minimal set: server TTFT p50/p95/p99, server TPOT p50/p95/p99, end-to-end p50/p95/p99, token throughput, GPU utilization, batch sizes distribution, queue length, and cache hit ratio. We'll provide a Grafana dashboard template.
04:59 Dana: ok. Security/compliance — we need to ensure data never leaves our VPC, KMS keys for model artifacts, and audit logs for every request. Can Redwood run Private in our VPC for the POC? 
05:12 Ethan: yes we can do a short-lived private deployment (customer-managed VPC) for the POC or run on Redwood dedicated with strict network peering. We'll share the VPC reference architecture. Also we'll surface SOC2 doc and key management integrations.
05:25 Ayesha: great. For instrumentation we also want a request ID correlated across client logs and Redwood logs. 
05:31 Priya: we support passing x-request-id and we'll include that in the perf traces.
05:35 Marco: sampling ratio — when replaying production, we might not want to push 100% of traffic. How do we pick a representative subset? 
05:41 Liam: pick stratified sampling by payload bucket and user cohort. We'll bootstrap from your 7‑day histogram and sample proportional to real traffic, but oversample rare heavy payloads to get better tail estimates. 
05:55 Ayesha: timeline — we want baseline within two weeks. Can Redwood run baseline and two full sweep tests in that window? 
06:01 Ethan: yes, if we get logs and histogram by 2026-07-26 we can schedule the baseline run week of 2026-08-03 and a follow-up optimization run week of 2026-08-10. 
06:11 Dana: what about model variants — we sometimes run quantized vs fp16 models. Should we test both? 
06:16 Priya: definitely. We'll recommended quantized variants for cost testing. Our Optimize team will pick two model configs: standard float and int8 quantized, and run the same sample set to compare TTFT/TPOT and quality regressions.
06:30 Marco: quality checks — how do we ensure quantization doesn't regress user visible outputs? 
06:34 Liam: include a small eval set of prompts with expected outputs. We'll run BLEU-like and human spot-checks. For the POC we suggest a pass/fail threshold: no more than X% degradation on chosen metrics — we'll define that in the playbook.
06:48 Ayesha: can we also test prefix caching effects? Our flows reuse context a lot. 
06:52 Priya: yes we'll include cache-warm scenarios. For sampling we'll include sequences with repeated user sessions to show KV cache hit rate and how TTFT improves.
07:00 Dana: excellent. Anything else on measurement? 
07:03 Ethan: one more piece — measurement windows. For p95 sampling we need sufficiently large sample sizes. For small payloads that's easy; for large/rare payloads we need to run longer or oversample. We'll recommend minimum 500 samples for p95 PD reliability and 5k for p99 if feasible. 
07:23 Marco: ok makes sense. If we can't reach 5k large samples, we accept wider confidence intervals. 
07:29 Priya: we'll capture confidence intervals in the dashboard.
07:33 Ayesha: last question — reporting format and artifacts we'll get? 
07:36 Ethan: we'll deliver a benchmark report with raw CSVs, dashboard links, and a short executive summary. Also we'll include a recommended configuration set for Dedicated or Private deployment.
07:47 Dana: sounds good. Let's recap next steps. 
07:50 Ethan: recap: Redwood sends sampling script + playbook, Polar sends histogram and sample logs, Redwood provisions test cluster, baseline run week of 8/3. We'll also exchange SOC2 docs and VPC arch. 
08:04 Ayesha: agreed. Thanks everyone. 

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hears (e.g., 'JMX-style' could be 'JMeter-style'), speaker labels approximate.

References shared during call: (1) Redwood sampling script repo (placeholder) https://redwood.internal/samples/payload-playbook (2) Benchmark spreadsheet TBD link will be shared after ACL.
